input_roles.role: exact vehicle target; conventional mirror-like device replaced by flush camera optics

prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: M11 futuristic truck exterior detail correction R3.
Input image 1 is the exact edit target, current R2 truck. Preserve the entire vehicle's design, four axles, one detached-capable cargo container, ivory/navy/orange palette, cab windshield/nose shapes, perspective and crisp anime mechanical rendering. Do NOT redesign truck.
Correct ONLY the rear-view devices and add a subtle equipment-bay seam:
1. REMOVE the small projecting mirror-like black rectangular housing and its short support from the near A-pillar/cab side, and remove any conventional far-side external mirror if present. No reflective glass mirror plates or mirror stalks anywhere.
2. Instead place a TINY FLUSH dark camera window integrated INTO the existing near A-pillar / side body at the same functional position. Its small aperture contains two unmistakable circular camera LENSES and no reflective mirror surface. The whole window is flush or only gently proud of the ivory body, with no lateral wing/stalk. Far-side equivalent is naturally mostly occluded. It must read as camera optics, not a miniature wing mirror.
3. At the rear-central cab roof, add only a discreet rectangular service-hatch seam flush with the aerodynamic roof. This is the robot-head/antenna equipment bay in vehicle mode; keep the roof low and smooth, no antenna sticking up in vehicle mode, no extra hump or exterior robot head.
Composition: main complete truck in same front-left three-quarter position, with a SMALL separate closeup inset in unused upper-left background showing the near flush TWO-LENS camera window clearly, connected by a thin simple leader line. This inset is a detail view of the same body patch, NOT another mirror or second vehicle. No text.
Keep all four near-side road wheels visible/countable, no extra wheels, no new armament or lighting strip redesign. Warm white plain background, soft ground shadow. No Tesla logo or other branding, typography, watermark, or geometric style change.
